newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight steady at 6.5/8 pct despite liquidity.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight steady at 6.5/8 pct despite liquidity.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was unchanged at 6.5/8 percent despite a mild improvement in liquidity which earlier pulled down other interbank rates, dealers said on Tuesday.
They said the there was pressure on the overnight rate due to improved funds flow on the back of a strengthening ringgit.
"The rate could still go down to around 6.0 percent," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
Earlier, other interbank rates eased across a wide front.
The dealers said one-week interbank rate eased to 6.90/7.00 percent against 7.20/25 at close on Monday, while one-month was down to 7.20/25 percent against 7.33/35.
Two-week money was at 7.00/10 percent against 7.25/30, three-week at 7.10/20 against 7.30/35, three-month at 7.25/30 against 7.35/38 and six-month unchanged at 7.35/40.
"Swaps are cheaper this morning, which indicates that foreign funds are coming in. That is pressuring rates downward," said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank.
The ringgit has gained sharply since Monday against the U.S. dollar. It has risen to a four-month high of 2.4940/50 a dollar overnight against 2.5218 at close on Friday.
With the ringgit's sharp gains, more funds are expected to come in over the next few days.
Dealers said higher interest rates in Malaysia, a sharply improved trade balance figure and movement from Singapore dollar to ringgit was helping the Malaysian unit.
The three-month benchmark rate in Malaysia was around four percentage points higher than in Singapore.
Dealers said demand for the 10-year government bond continued on Tuesday with prices rising to a high of 100.80 ringgit before settling at 100.72/80 against 100.50/53 previously.
The demand for the bond was both speculative and for meeting reserve requirements. The rise in the price was due to the lack of many sellers in the market.
